title: Verbatim finder for General Comments
problem:
GOAL AND WHY
When I write a submission on [my topic], I need the exact words of UN treaty bodies' General Comments, with a correct citation. A chatbot's paraphrase is not enough: I have to quote.

BEFORE YOU BUILD
Look at the attached file and tell me what it contains and what it lacks. Then write a plan. Do not build anything until I approve the plan.

LIMITS
Use only the attached file. Never shorten or rewrite a paragraph. Nothing leaves my browser.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
I type a phrase and see every paragraph that contains it, word for word, each with its document symbol and paragraph number. I can copy a ready citation.

CHECK BEFORE YOU FINISH
Show how many paragraphs were searched. Say what the tool cannot do.
facilitator_brief: A search tool over every General Comment paragraph of the treaty bodies, for one participant's topic: it retrieves, it never generates. A plan short enough to read and debate in pairs in three minutes.
notes:
Your prompt asks for a retrieval tool, not a writing tool: the exact words of General Comments on your topic, with a citation a reader can check, and nothing leaving your browser. I take the facilitator's line as the rule: the tool retrieves, it never generates.

 The file holds 7,304 paragraphs, each with a symbol, paragraph number, committee, year, title, link and text; only `cited_articles` is often empty. There are 159 symbols but 188 titles, so some symbols hold more than one document.  Ten committees, very unevenly: CRC 2,091 paragraphs, CEDAW 1,306, CESCR 1,222, down to CED with 56. A topic outside the CRC's field will have fewer hits; that is the file, not the tool.  "best interests" gives 641 matches, and the lines show curly apostrophes (child’s): matching must treat ’ and ' alike, and the app must count paragraphs, not occurrences, so its number will be lower.  The list of symbols shows five joint General Comments with two symbols in one field (CMW/C/GC/7–CERD/C/GC/38) and annual reports such as A/48/18 that hold several General Recommendations. The citation must copy the symbol as stored and add the short title where a symbol is shared.   The Dag Hammarskjöld Library says no single citation style is prescribed; a good citation carries the symbol, the pinpoint, the title and the date. So the fields stay separate and I ask you which form to copy.

I decided on one screen, no filters, three example searches and a draft list. I leave three things to you: what counts as a match, how the citation reads, and what a result shows first. Debate them; a wrong default costs you a quotation.

plan_base:
# Verbatim finder: {topic}

## What you asked for

You need the exact words of General Comments on {topic}, with a citation a reader can check: from the attached file only, never summarised; nothing leaves your browser.

## What I found in the file

- About 7,300 paragraphs from ten committees, 1972–2026, every field filled.
- Uneven: CRC about 2,100 paragraphs, CED about 60.
- Trap: a `symbol` is not always one document: A/48/18 holds seven General Recommendations; five joint General Comments carry two symbols in one field (CMW/C/GC/7–CERD/C/GC/38).
- `text` keeps curly apostrophes (child’s) and footnote marks like [[fn:12]]; "best interests" occurs 641 times.

## What the tool will do

One screen: a search box, three example searches about {topic} as buttons, and "N paragraphs searched" always visible (count `records`).

{{q1}}

Results: {{q3}} Each result: `committee`, `short_title`, `symbol` linked to `doc_url`, para. `paragraph`, the full `text` as stored, and two buttons. "Copy citation" {{q2}} "Add to draft" puts it in a draft list below ("Copy all", "Download"). No match: say so, show 0.

## Your decisions

- Matching. {{q1.decision}}
- Citation. {{q2.decision}}
- Results. {{q3.decision}}

## Look

{look}

## What it will not do

- No summaries, paraphrase or synonyms: only the words you typed.
- No other sources: no concluding observations, no case law.
- No translation: English only.

## How you can check it

1. Search, in quotation marks, a phrase you know: it appears in a result word for word, apostrophes included.
2. Click a result's symbol (`doc_url`) and compare the paragraph with the original.
3. Click "Copy citation", paste it into any document: symbol and paragraph number as the result showed them.
